court-06.claim: The Supreme Court's judgment of 27 May 2026 records that some petitions, W.P.(C) 855 of 2025 among them, were filed in support of the revision and asked for it to be held at regular intervals.

court-09.case: Petitions including the DMK's against the order of 27 October 2025, Supreme Court

court-11.note: National Herald page fetched; published 4 Dec 2025. The quoted line is the reporter's paraphrase of what the Bench observed, not in quotation marks, and reads like the Court's words. Replaced with the report's own factual sentence. The report says the Court 'suggested' more staff and shorter hours, so 'told' is softened, and the deaths are as alleged in TVK's application.
court-11.claim: On a TVK application saying 35 to 40 booth level officers had died under work pressure, the Court suggested that states provide more staff and cut working hours in proportion, National Herald reported.
court-11.quote: The court suggested that states supply additional manpower to lighten workloads and reduce working hours proportionately.

court-13.note: LiveLaw page fetched. Quote is from the Bench's order as quoted, verbatim. Claim matches; the petitioner is a private individual and is rightly not named. The report is dated 2025-12-18 (order on Wednesday 17 December), so the date is corrected.

court-14.note: Order dated 19-01-2026 read. Para 2: 'approximately 1.40 crore individuals have been issued notices'. Quote verbatim from para 4(i).

court-15.note: Order dated 09-02-2026 read. Para 2 records that on 04.02.2026 Ms. Mamata Banerjee appeared along with her senior counsel in W.P.(C) 129 of 2026 filed by her. 8505 Group B officers offered by the State. Quote verbatim from para 6(i).

court-16.note: LawTrend page fetched. The petition was filed on 10 February but the report is dated February 12, 2026, so the date is corrected. Claim matches the reliefs sought. Quote verbatim.

court-17.note: Verdictum page fetched; dated 23 Feb 2026. 91 residents displaced in September 2023. Quote is the Bench's order as quoted, verbatim. Liberty to approach the High Court confirmed. Petitioners not named in the claim.

court-18.note: Order dated 10-03-2026 read. Quote verbatim (para 10). The 10,16,000+ figure is the Calcutta High Court Chief Justice's report as recorded in the order, so the claim now says so. The Court requested the Chief Justice to nominate former Chief Justices and judges, to be notified by the Commission as Appellate Tribunals.
court-18.claim: The Court recorded the Chief Justice of the Calcutta High Court's report that over 10,16,000 objections had been disposed of, and directed that appeals against the judicial officers' orders go to tribunals of former Chief Justices and judges.

court-19.note: Order dated 02-04-2026 read. Quote verbatim. The order says seven judicial officers were 'gheraoed' at the BDO office in Kaliachowk, Maldah, and directs the ECI to entrust the inquiry to 'an independent agency, such as' the CBI or NIA. 'held' replaced by 'surrounded' and 'asked' by 'directed' to match.
court-19.claim: After seven judicial officers deciding SIR objections were surrounded at a BDO office in Maldah district, the Court directed central forces for them and directed the Commission to give the inquiry to an independent agency such as the CBI or the NIA.

court-20.note: Order dated 13-04-2026 read. Quote verbatim (para 11). The order does not describe the W.P.(C) 462 petitioners as deleted after the judicial officers' check; it says they had already filed an appeal. The supplementary roll covers appeals decided by 21.04.2026 or 27.04.2026.
court-20.claim: The Court directed that appeals the tribunals decided by 21 or 27 April 2026, before polling, be given effect in a supplementary roll, and said a pending appeal gave no right to vote.

court-21.note: Supreme Court Observer page fetched; dated 24 Apr 2026. Senior Advocate Kalyan Banerjee said 136 of nearly 27 lakh appeals had been disposed of. Quote is the CJI's words, verbatim.

court-22.note: Judgment 2026 INSC 564 read. Para 186(a) holds the exercise 'traceable to Section 21(3) of the RP Act read with Article 324'. Quote verbatim from para 176 (page 117).

court-23.note: Judgment para 186(h) read. Quote verbatim. The same paragraph lets persons domiciled in Bihar erroneously deleted as absent, dead, shifted or in duplication seek judicial review.

court-24.note: Telangana High Court order in W.P. No. 20188 of 2026, dated 30.06.2026, read from the LiveLaw upload. Petitioner a voter of AC 218 Charminar seeking restoration of his and his family's names; petition dismissed. Quote verbatim (a page number breaks the text in the PDF). Petitioner rightly not named.

court-25.note: Telangana Today page fetched; dated 6 August 2026. Quote verbatim. The report describes the voters as 'allegedly illegal', so the claim attributes the word ineligible to the petitioner.
court-25.claim: Adivasi Sena asked the Telangana High Court to have non-tribal voters it called ineligible deleted from the rolls of the Fifth Schedule Areas during the revision, and the Court sought replies, Telangana Today reported.

court-26.note: Telangana Today page fetched; dated 6 August 2026. Quote verbatim; it is the petitioners' contention as reported, which the claim attributes to the petitioners. Listed to 12 August after the Commission sought time.

The live headline differs from the item's ('How Can We Monitor?' Delhi High Court Reserves Verdict On PIL To Include Homeless, Demolition-Displaced Persons In SIR).

court-28.note: LiveLaw page fetched; dated 20 Aug 2026. Quote verbatim. Court did not examine the merits. Petitioner not named.

court-29.note: LiveLaw page fetched; dated 10 Sept 2026. Petition by Devender Yadav (DPCC president) and a DPCC office-bearer. Justice Amit Bansal asked them to file a PIL; quote verbatim.

court-30.note: ThePrint (PTI) page fetched; dated 22 September 2026. PIL by Anjali Bhardwaj and Amrita Johri sought the list of noticed voters and the logical-discrepancy criteria. Quote verbatim.

court-31.note: LiveLaw page fetched; dated 5 Oct 2026. Petition sought quashing of 14 decisions 'allegedly taken unilaterally'; notice issued and tagged with a similar matter. Quote is the CJI's words, verbatim. Petitioner not named in the claim.

court-32.note: The Wire page fetched; published 1 Oct 2026 11:46, hearing Wednesday 30 September, headline matches. Both quoted passages verbatim (the second is The Wire quoting TOI). The response matches the Wire's account of the Commission's counsel. Telangana Today (PTI, 1 Oct 11:18) agrees on the six family members, Santa Cruz, Form 8 and ERONET offering only 'reject', and attributes that account to the petitioners ('they said'); the claim stated it as fact, so it is restated as what the family told the court. Case number confirmed from LiveLaw's case details (Writ Petition 732 of 2026). No private person named in claim, quote or response.
court-32.claim: A family of six told the court that they had moved house within the same constituency and filed Form 8 on a BLO's instruction, and that they were then deleted from the roll because the ERONET software found no record of their cards and allowed only a rejection. The bench asked the Commission to show where the law allows a deletion without a hearing and said the family should not have been asked to file Form 6, The Wire reported, citing The Times of India.

court-33.note: LiveLaw page fetched; published 5 Oct 2026 18:38, hearing Monday 5 October, headline matches the page title. Case details at the foot give Writ Petition 732 of 2026. Both quoted passages verbatim, the second attributed to Justice Menezes. Claim and response match the report (ECI counsel argued the enumeration form must go with Form 8, else Form 6). The page names the petitioning family; the item does not.

court-34.note: LiveLaw page fetched; published 5 Oct 2026 17:04, headline matches. Quotes verbatim. Claim matches: the Chief Justice's bench declined the oral prayer that no names be deleted, said it would follow the Supreme Court's November restraint as it was informed, adjourned four weeks; the petition seeks the order and recorded reasons and safeguards against wrongful exclusion. court-35.note: Merged from two second readings of 2026-10-10. LiveLaw 553920 opened: quote in the order as reproduced, 57 Metro stations from 9 PM on 9 October verified, New Delhi and Nizamuddin trains between 4 AM and 2 PM on 10 October is Kapil Sibal's statement, the Solicitor General's 'far from the truth' verified as reported speech, petition by CPI(M) General Secretary MA Baby and others. ETV Bharat (Sumit Saxena, 9 Oct 2026 5:21 pm) opened: the order's word is 'overreaching' and the bench asked the Centre to reconsider Jantar Mantar as the designated protest site. ETV's report put the Solicitor General's remark that a protest was unlawful without permission beside this order, but that remark was about the earlier Congress protest, so it is left out.

court-36.note: Outlook (News Desk, 10 Oct 2026 11:15 am) opened in full. 'persisted with unwarranted train cancellations' is verbatim inside the plea's longer sentence, quoted here in full. 57 stations and the three named officials verified. The page adds that the 9 October order sought a compliance report within four days and directed a traffic advisory in newspapers, and the plea says none was published. No hearing reported.

court-37.quote: the applicants claim that their names were deleted without any notice to them.

court-38.note: LiveLaw AMP opened (curl, full text served), 9 Oct 2026. Quote verbatim. Figures are counsel's: 93% of nearly 1 lakh decided appeals restored, nearly 1.70 lakh pending, an interim order sought to let appellants vote. The Chief Justice's line that appeals by persons seeking deletion 'can be pushed behind and taken last' verified, and 29 October offered as the alternative date.

court-39.claim: The Supreme Court, hearing a challenge to the Andhra Pradesh High Court's order for local body elections within six weeks, said the elections should use the revised roll if it is published before the polls are notified, and the existing roll if it is not. It said the roll in force applies until the Commission publishes the revised list and that the revision cannot be a reason to delay the polls.
court-39.quote: However, if the final SIR rolls were not published before the notification, the elections would be conducted using the existing electoral rolls in accordance with the applicable State laws.
court-39.response: The bench noted that the Election Commission had proposed to publish the final roll on 16 October 2026. Senior Advocate K Parameshwar, for the State Election Commission, said the rolls in force continue until the Commission publishes a fresh list.
court-39.note: LiveLaw opened; the clarification paragraphs are served in full. Claim tightened to what the bench said while hearing a challenge to the High Court's order of 1 October. The Court did not set aside or modify the High Court's six-week direction in the text served. 16 October is what the bench noted the Commission had proposed. 44 lakh is Senior Advocate C Aryama Sundaram's submission for the petitioner.

court-41.case: Writ Petition No. 732 of 2026, a family's petition on deletion after Form 8, Bombay High Court at Goa
court-41.claim: The Bombay High Court at Goa adjourned the St Cruz family's petition by a week at the Commission's request, after the Commission said orders the Supreme Court might pass could bear on it. The judges took the view that the Supreme Court's orders may not have a direct bearing, PTI reported, and the Commission's advocate told reporters the Supreme Court had asked High Courts to defer such hearings.
court-41.note: ThePrint (PTI, 6 Oct 2026, Tuesday) opened. Same petition as court-32 and court-33 (WP 732 of 2026), so that case string is used. The statement that the Supreme Court had told High Courts to defer such hearings was made by the Commission's advocate to reporters, and the bench's own view was that the Supreme Court's orders may not bear directly on the case. Both are now in the claim. Adjourned to 'next Tuesday', 13 October. The family is named in the article and is not named here.
